_comment: The ONE table of cases for the export CSV's round trip, read by BOTH sides of it:
server/src/modules/account/export-csv.spec.ts WRITES these rows and
composeApp/src/commonTest/.../ExportRoundTripTest.kt READS them back through M3's
importer. FR-SET-03 produces the file; FR-IMP-04..08 consume it; definition-of-done
item 2 is the claim that the two agree.
MILESTONE_CHECKLIST.md, bought by M3: 'a rule implemented TWICE in TWO languages is
held to one shared table of cases'. The export format is exactly that shape — a writer
in TypeScript and a reader in Kotlin — and nothing else would notice them drifting,
because each side's own tests pass perfectly while disagreeing with the other.
## Why the dates are written as `d MMM yyyy` and not `dd/MM/yyyy`
Because `03/05/1990` is AMBIGUOUS and the importer resolves it with a USER PREFERENCE.
FR-IMP-06's dd/MM-vs-MM/dd toggle defaults to day-first for India, and FR-SET-08 makes
it a setting the user can change — so an export written as `03/05/1990` re-imports as
3 May for one user and 5 March for another. A round trip that depends on a preference
is not a round trip; it is silent data corruption for whoever flipped the switch.
`ImportDates.fromNamedMonth` returns `ambiguous = false` unconditionally, because a
named month leaves nothing to be ambiguous about. So `3 May 1990` reads identically
under either setting, which is the property this format was chosen for.
## Why the header is exactly this
Definition-of-done item 2 says 'without a mapping change', which means
`ImportStore.guessMapping` has to claim all five columns correctly with nobody
touching the screen. It matches on substrings in claim order (name, date, relation,
phone, notes), and one column may only be claimed once. `expectedMapping` below is
asserted against the real guesser rather than assumed.
Every person here is INVENTED. The repo is public (MILESTONE_CHECKLIST.md §F).

cases.why: the base case — every field present, year known
FR-EVT-02 — year unknown must survive the trip as unknown, not as a guess
both numbers under 13 — the case dd/MM/yyyy would resolve differently under each setting of the FR-SET-08 toggle
a comma in a note — the quoting rule, which is where two CSV implementations differ first
a double quote inside a note — doubled on write, collapsed on read
a newline inside a note — the case a line-based reader gets wrong and a real CSV reader does not
a comma in the NAME, which is also what a dedup rule tokenises

_notInThisFile: DEATH ANNIVERSARIES AND SECOND EVENTS ARE NOT HERE, AND THAT IS THE POINT.
and ColumnMapping has five targets with no type among them. So one row is one person
and one BIRTHDAY, always. A death anniversary written into this file and re-imported
would come back as a birthday — the outcome FR-EVT-05 calls 'the worst failure this
app can have ... impossible by construction, not by a copy tweak'.
The export therefore writes ONLY birthdays to people.csv, says so in the file itself,
and puts every event of every type in the JSON, which is the lossless artifact.
docs/M9_PLAN.md C11 raises this rather than resolving it: the alternative readings of
